definitions.gloss: second generation; successor; the second to hold a title or position
definitions.explanation: The second person to hold a particular name, title, or leadership position, especially in family businesses, traditional arts, or hereditary roles. Composed of {二|に} (two) + {代目|だいめ} (generation-counter).

examples.japanese: {二代目|にだいめ}が{店|みせ}を{継|つ}いだ。
examples.english: The second-generation owner took over the shop.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{二代目|にだいめ}{社長|しゃちょう}として{会社|かいしゃ}を{大|おお}きくした。
examples.english: As the second-generation president, he grew the company.

examples.japanese: この{老舗|しにせ}は{二代目|にだいめ}の{時代|じだい}に{全国的|ぜんこくてき}に{名|な}が{知|し}られるようになった。
examples.english: This long-established shop became nationally known during the second generation's era.

notes:
USAGE:
{二代目|にだいめ} can be used on its own to refer to the successor, or before a title: {二代目|にだいめ}{社長|しゃちょう} (second-generation president). The pattern extends to other numbers: {三代目|さんだいめ} (third generation), {初代|しょだい} (the first/founding generation). In traditional performing arts like {歌舞伎|かぶき}, stage names are inherited across generations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {二代目|にだいめ}{社長|しゃちょう} (second-generation company president)
- {二代目|にだいめ}を{継|つ}ぐ (succeed as the second generation)
- {二代目|にだいめ}が{店|みせ}を{継|つ}ぐ (the successor takes over the shop)

RELATED TERMS:
- {初代|しょだい} refers to the founder or first holder of a title.
- {三代目|さんだいめ} is the third generation.
- {跡継|あとつ}ぎ is a general term for successor or heir.
